szoveg_eredeti:
By Ayana Birbayeva in Editor’s Picks, International on 26 November 2026

ASTANA – Kazakhstan and Russia are advancing cooperation in artificial intelligence and high-tech industries as bilateral trade approaches $30 billion, President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and Russian President Vladimir Putin said during a Nov. 25 meeting in the Kremlin ahead of the AI Journey 2026 conference.

From L to R: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and Russian President Vladimir Putin. Photo credit: Akorda.

Tokayev highlighted the growing importance of artificial intelligence and digitalization, recalling that Putin had outlined during the first AI Journey forum in 2020 that these technologies would soon become global priorities.

“Now everyone is talking about high technologies, artificial intelligence, and how it will behave in the future,” Tokayev said, emphasizing the significance of the upcoming forum.

According to him, Kazakhstan has made digitalization and artificial intelligence a national priority, with 2026 declared the Year of Artificial Intelligence Development. Tokayev said the country had made progress in digital transformation, citing its 16th-place ranking in the United Nations e-government and human capital development assessment, up from 24th.

Tokayev said Kazakhstan and Russia were steadily moving toward a bilateral trade turnover of $30 billion. He noted that the intergovernmental commission was working to implement agreements reached during Putin’s state visit to Kazakhstan in May, which led to the signing of several important documents.

Tokayev also commented on the recent trilateral meeting involving the leaders of China, the United States and Russia in Shenzhen, noting that it took place amid a highly volatile geopolitical situation. He said Russia’s participation in the meeting as a major global power was a significant achievement for Putin.

“The declaration was adopted, and it is absolutely optimal in terms of its content and, of course, its significance, because it would be unrealistic to expect anything more in this modern world,” he said.

He also noted that the declaration’s wording and substance reflected ideas Putin had previously discussed, adding that the declaration represented a significant achievement for Russian diplomacy.

Putin thanked Tokayev for visiting Russia and accepting the invitation to attend the AI Journey conference. He said the event would provide an opportunity to hear from specialists, meet with schoolchildren and university students, and discuss cooperation between Russia and Kazakhstan in high-tech industries, particularly artificial intelligence.

The presidents discussed further development of trade, economic and investment cooperation, as well as joint projects in energy, industry, agriculture, transport and logistics. They also exchanged views on current international and regional issues.
